I'll check what your training has looked like before answering. I can't see any logged training or an active program on my end, so I can't judge your load from numbers. I'll go off what you've told me instead.

Eight hard weeks is right around when a lighter week starts to pay off. Whether you need one depends on how you're trending. Reasons to take it: your lifts have stalled or slipped for a couple of weeks, warm-ups feel heavy, your sleep or motivation has dipped, or sessions feel harder at the same weights. If you're still hitting your numbers and feeling good, you can keep going, though a planned deload every 6 to 8 weeks is a sensible habit either way.

A typical deload keeps the same exercises and movement patterns but cuts the volume to roughly half and leaves a few more reps in the tank. You come back fresher, not detrained.

How have your main lifts been moving over the last couple of weeks? If you'd like, I can build you a lighter session or week to run it.
